summary: Contains the latest ARPANET maps, geographic and logical, from early 1974. The original consisted of two one-page illustrations that cannot be reproduced in ASCII text.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 616 contains two ARPANET maps for January 1974: one geographic and one logical. The text version includes the map titles but does not reproduce the full illustrations.

subtitle: Geographic and logical maps of the ARPANET in January 1974.

tldr.problem: Readers and operators needed visual references for the ARPANET's geographic and logical layout.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 616 distributes two maps labeled as the geographic and logical ARPANET maps for January 1974.
tldr.outcome: The RFC is a map document; the text extraction preserves the labels but not the full map illustrations.

today: RFC 616 is an archival document containing geographic and logical ARPANET maps dated January 1974.

sections.title: Two ARPANET Maps
sections.content: The RFC is titled “Latest Network Maps” and includes a geographic map and a logical map of the ARPANET. Both map headings identify January 1974 as the map date.
sections.plainLanguage: The document contains two kinds of ARPANET map, both dated January 1974. One is geographic and the other is logical.

sections.title: Geographic and Logical Views
sections.content: The geographic map is labeled as a map of the ARPA Network. The second is labeled as the logical map. The RFC presents them as illustrations rather than describing their contents in prose.
sections.plainLanguage: The two illustrations present different views of the ARPANET. The text does not explain individual map details.

sections.title: A Dated Map Record
sections.content: The RFC records a pair of network maps with January 1974 headings. The extracted text includes some place and site labels, but the maps themselves carry the visual information.
sections.plainLanguage: This RFC preserves a dated map snapshot of the network. Its text alone does not show the complete maps.
